_readme: Every setting for bike-buddy. Edit, then reload it WITHOUT recompiling:
Read through the shared appcfg.h loader. Any key may be left out -- the
firmware default applies. A value outside its allowed range is REJECTED and
named on the serial log, not silently clamped.
There are no secrets in this app at all: no Wi-Fi, no API keys, nothing to
put in secrets.h. That is the point of the design -- see the README on why
the iPhone is deliberately not in the loop.
Several keys here are CALIBRATION, not preference. A bike computer that
cannot be calibrated to the actual bike reports confident wrong numbers,
which is worse than reporting none.
_units: 'metric' or 'imperial'. Affects display only; the log is always SI.
_wheel: Rolling circumference in millimetres, 800-2500. CALIBRATION, and the most
important number in this file: every distance and every wheel-sensor speed
MEASURE IT. Mark the tyre, roll the bike one full rotation with your weight
on it, measure the marks. Do not use the size printed on the sidewall --
tyre width, pressure and rider weight move this by a couple of percent, and
a couple of percent is a wrong distance on every ride forever.
2136 is a 29x2.4 at trail pressure, which is a starting point and not an
_speed: 'auto' prefers the CSC wheel sensor and falls back to GPS when it drops.
That is the right default under tree cover, where GPS speed lags a second
or two and goes noisy -- which is exactly the terrain this device is for.
GPS still owns distance-along-route and position regardless.
_barometer: Elevation and live grade come from the BMP280, not from GPS. GPS altitude
is the worst number GPS produces -- plus or minus 10-20m, and it wanders
while you stand still, which makes both total ascent and live grade junk.
zeroAtStart   take the trailhead as the reference on boot.
seaLevelHpa   used when zeroAtStart is false, 950-1050. CALIBRATION: this
drifts with the weather over a single day, which is why it is
a setting and not a constant.
gradeWindowM  distance over which grade is averaged, 10-200. Too short and
the number flickers on every root; too long and it lags the
_sensors: BLE MAC addresses of the sensors to connect to, as a plain allow-list.
Empty string means 'not fitted' and the field simply does not draw.
These are standard GATT profiles -- heart rate 0x180D, cadence and wheel
speed 0x1816, power 0x1818 -- so any mainstream strap or sensor works and
there is no vendor cloud in the path. Naming them by MAC rather than
scanning-and-picking keeps the pairing UX at zero, which matters on a
device with no keyboard and one tap gesture.
Straps also report their own battery over BAS 0x180F; that is what the
SYSTEM page shows, since the board itself runs off a dumb USB bank with no
_imu: enabled     the accelerometer and gyro are optional; everything else works
airtimeG    freefall threshold as a fraction of g, 0.1-0.5. Total
acceleration below this counts as airborne.
airtimeMs   how long it has to stay there to count as a jump, 50-1000.
Suspension mutes the first few milliseconds, so airtime is
measured from the threshold crossing, not from takeoff.
LEAN ANGLE DOES NOT COME FROM THE ACCELEROMETER. It is atan(v * yawRate /
g) -- a bike leans until lateral g reads about zero, so a car-style g-meter
would sit dead still through the best corner of the ride. See the README.
Impact detection flags the ride log. It is NOT crash detection: there is no
connectivity here to call anyone with.
_pages: default        which page to sit on: map, climb, numbers, trip, system.
autoClimb      switch to CLIMB when a climb starts and back when it tops
out. Free, because the climbs are precomputed on the host.
Tapping away from CLIMB suppresses it for that climb --
automatic help that overrides a deliberate action stops
returnSeconds  bounce back to 'default' after this long on SYSTEM or TRIP,
0-600, 0 to disable. Stops you descending a mountain looking
_autopause: TWO thresholds, not one. A single threshold flickers between moving and
stopped on a slow technical climb and ruins the moving average.
pauseBelowKph   stop the moving timer under this, 0.5-10.
resumeAboveKph  start it again over this, 1-20. Must exceed pauseBelowKph;
dwellMs         how long the condition must hold either way, 500-10000.
_route: gpx   the planned route, drawn on MAP.
prof  distance/elevation pairs sampled from the DEM at prep time, plus the
precomputed climb list. Under 5KB for a 30km route, and it is the
ENTIRE input to the CLIMB page -- no tiles involved, which is why
that page ships before the map does.
offRouteM  how far off the line before the page stops counting down to a
summit and says OFF ROUTE instead, 10-500. Distance-to-top is
meaningless once you are not on the route, and a confident wrong
number is the failure mode this whole repo guards against.
Both empty means free-ride: breadcrumb and numbers, no route, no climbs.
_map: tileDir  where the prepared JPEG tiles live on the card.
zoom     16 puts a tile at roughly 400m at mid-latitudes; a 10km square is
Tiles are RENDERED locally from an OSM extract plus a DEM, not downloaded:
tile servers' usage policies forbid bulk fetching, and more to the point
you cannot restyle somebody else's PNG. The styling -- hillshade base,
index contours only, trails coloured by mtb:scale -- is the whole reason
_brightness: min, max  the range it maps between, 8-255.
NOTE THE HIGH FLOOR. This is an outdoor device: the failure mode is a
washed-out screen in direct sun, not a too-bright one at night. Power is
not scarce here -- a 5000mAh bank runs this about 20 hours -- so there is
Do NOT add a sleep or deep-dim mode without checking your power bank. Most
banks cut output below ~50-70mA. The device draws 120-180mA, so it is
clear -- but 'saving power' can drop it under the threshold and the bank
_log: flushSeconds  how often the track log is flushed to the card, 1-60.
The log is appended one line per fix and flushed on this interval rather
than held open, because losing power mid-write can take the filesystem
down with it. A truncated append-only log is still a valid partial ride;
